entries.originalText: Moreover, ye were all distinguished by humility, and were in no respect puffed up with pride, but yielded obedience rather than extorted it, and were more willing to give than to receive.
entries.modernizedText: Moreover, you were all distinguished by humility, and were in no respect puffed up with pride, but yielded obedience rather than extorted it, and were more willing to give than to receive.

entries.originalText: Content with the provision which God had made for you, and carefully attending to His words, ye were inwardly filled with His doctrine, and His sufferings were before your eyes.
entries.modernizedText: Content with the provision which God had made for you, and carefully attending to His words, you were inwardly filled with His doctrine, and His sufferings were before your eyes.

entries.originalText: Thus a profound and abundant peace was given to you all, and ye had an insatiable desire for doing good, while a full outpouring of the Holy Spirit was upon you all.
entries.modernizedText: Thus a profound and abundant peace was given to you all, and you had an insatiable desire for doing good, while a full outpouring of the Holy Spirit was upon you all.

entries.originalText: Full of holy designs, ye did, with true earnestness of mind and a godly confidence, stretch forth your hands to God Almighty, beseeching Him to be merciful unto you, if ye had been guilty of any involuntary transgression.
entries.modernizedText: Full of holy designs, you did, with true earnestness of mind and a godly confidence, stretch forth your hands to God Almighty, beseeching Him to be merciful to you, if you had been guilty of any involuntary transgression.

entries.originalText: Day and night ye were anxious for the whole brotherhood, that the number of God’s elect might be saved with mercy and a good conscience.
entries.modernizedText: Day and night you were anxious for the whole brotherhood, that God’s elect might be saved with mercy and a good conscience.

entries.originalText: Ye were sincere and uncorrupted, and forgetful of injuries between one another.
entries.modernizedText: You were sincere and uncorrupted, and forgetful of injuries between one another.

entries.originalText: Every kind of faction and schism was abominable in your sight.
entries.modernizedText: Every kind of faction and schism was abominable in your sight.

entries.originalText: Ye mourned over the transgressions of your neighbours: their deficiencies you deemed your own.
entries.modernizedText: You mourned over the transgressions of your neighbors: their deficiencies you deemed your own.

entries.originalText: Ye never grudged any act of kindness, being “ready to every good work.”
entries.modernizedText: You never grudged any act of kindness, being “ready to every good work.”

entries.originalText: Adorned by a thoroughly virtuous and religious life, ye did all things in the fear of God.
entries.modernizedText: Adorned by a thoroughly virtuous and religious life, you did all things in the fear of God.

entries.originalText: The commandments and ordinances of the Lord were written upon the tablets of your hearts.
entries.modernizedText: The commandments and ordinances of the Lord were written upon the tablets of your hearts.

entries.originalText: Every kind of honour and happiness was bestowed upon you, and then was fulfilled that which is written, “My beloved did eat and drink, and was enlarged and became fat, and kicked.”
entries.modernizedText: Every kind of honor and happiness was bestowed upon you, and then was fulfilled that which is written, “My beloved did eat and drink, and was enlarged and became fat, and kicked.”

entries.originalText: Hence flowed emulation and envy, strife and sedition, persecution and disorder, war and captivity.
entries.modernizedText: Hence flowed emulation and envy, strife and sedition, persecution and disorder, war and captivity.

entries.originalText: So the worthless rose up against the honoured, those of no reputation against such as were renowned, the foolish against the wise, the young against those advanced in years.
entries.modernizedText: So the worthless rose up against the honored, those of no reputation against such as were renowned, the foolish against the wise, the young against those advanced in years.

entries.originalText: For this reason righteousness and peace are now far departed from you, inasmuch as every one abandons the fear of God, and is become blind in His faith, neither walks in the ordinances of His appointment, nor acts a part becoming a Christian, but walks after his own wicked lusts, resuming the practice of an unrighteous and ungodly envy, by which death itself entered into the world.
entries.modernizedText: For this reason righteousness and peace are now far departed from you, inasmuch as everyone abandons the fear of God, and has become blind in His faith, neither walks in the ordinances of His appointment, nor acts in a manner becoming a Christian, but walks after his own wicked lusts, returning to the practice of unrighteous and ungodly envy, by which death itself entered into the world.

entries.originalText: For thus it is written: “And it came to pass after certain days, that Cain brought of the fruits of the earth a sacrifice unto God; and Abel also brought of the firstlings of his sheep, and of the fat thereof.
entries.modernizedText: For thus it is written: “And it came to pass after some days, that Cain brought of the fruits of the earth a sacrifice to God; and Abel also brought of the firstlings of his sheep, and of its fat.

entries.originalText: And God had respect to Abel and to his offerings, but Cain and his sacrifices He did not regard.
entries.modernizedText: And God had respect to Abel and to his offerings, but Cain and his sacrifices He did not regard.

entries.originalText: And Cain was deeply grieved, and his countenance fell.
entries.modernizedText: And Cain was deeply grieved, and his countenance fell.

entries.originalText: And God said to Cain, Why art thou grieved, and why is thy countenance fallen?
entries.modernizedText: And God said to Cain, Why are you grieved, and why is your countenance fallen?

entries.originalText: If thou offerest rightly, but dost not divide rightly, hast thou not sinned?
entries.modernizedText: If you offer rightly, but do not divide rightly, have you not sinned?

entries.originalText: Be at peace: thine offering returns to thyself, and thou shalt again possess it.
entries.modernizedText: Be at peace: your offering returns to you, and you shall again possess it.

entries.originalText: And Cain said to Abel his brother, Let us go into the field.
entries.modernizedText: And Cain said to Abel his brother, Let us go into the field.

entries.originalText: And it came to pass, while they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”
entries.modernizedText: And it came to pass, while they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”

entries.originalText: Ye see, brethren, how envy and jealousy led to the murder of a brother.
entries.modernizedText: You see, brethren, how envy and jealousy led to the murder of a brother.

entries.originalText: Through envy, also, our father Jacob fled from the face of Esau his brother.
entries.modernizedText: Through envy, also, our father Jacob fled from the face of Esau his brother.

entries.originalText: Envy made Joseph be persecuted unto death, and to come into bondage.
entries.modernizedText: Envy caused Joseph to be persecuted to death and brought into bondage.

entries.originalText: Envy compelled Moses to flee from the face of Pharaoh king of Egypt, when he heard these words from his fellow-countryman, “Who made thee a judge or a ruler over us?
entries.modernizedText: Envy compelled Moses to flee from the face of Pharaoh king of Egypt, when he heard these words from his fellow-countryman, “Who made you a judge or a ruler over us?

entries.originalText: Wilt thou kill me, as thou didst kill the Egyptian yesterday?”
entries.modernizedText: Will you kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?”

entries.originalText: On account of envy, Aaron and Miriam had to make their abode without the camp.
entries.modernizedText: On account of envy, Aaron and Miriam had to make their abode without the camp.

entries.originalText: Envy brought down Dathan and Abiram alive to Hades, through the sedition which they excited against God’s servant Moses.
entries.modernizedText: Envy brought down Dathan and Abiram alive to Hades, through the sedition which they excited against God’s servant Moses.

entries.originalText: Through envy, David not only underwent the hatred of foreigners, but was also persecuted by Saul king of Israel.
entries.modernizedText: Through envy, David not only underwent the hatred of foreigners, but was also persecuted by Saul king of Israel.

entries.originalText: But not to dwell upon ancient examples, let us come to the most recent spiritual heroes.
entries.modernizedText: But not to dwell upon ancient examples, let us come to the most recent spiritual heroes.

entries.originalText: Let us take the noble examples furnished in our own generation.
entries.modernizedText: Let us take the noble examples furnished in our own generation.

entries.originalText: Through envy and jealousy the greatest and most righteous pillars [of the church] have been persecuted and put to death.
entries.modernizedText: Through envy and jealousy the greatest and most righteous pillars [of the church] have been persecuted and put to death.

entries.originalText: Let us set before our eyes the illustrious apostles.
entries.modernizedText: Let us set before our eyes the illustrious apostles.

entries.originalText: Peter, through unrighteous envy, endured not one or two, but numerous labours; and when he had at length suffered martyrdom, departed to the place of glory due to him.
entries.modernizedText: Peter, through unrighteous envy, endured not one or two, but numerous labors; and when he had at length suffered martyrdom, departed to the place of glory due to him.

entries.originalText: Owing to envy, Paul also obtained the reward of patient endurance, after being seven times thrown into captivity, compelled to flee, and stoned.
entries.modernizedText: Owing to envy, Paul also obtained the reward of patient endurance, after being seven times thrown into captivity, compelled to flee, and stoned.

entries.originalText: After preaching both in the east and west, he gained the illustrious reputation due to his faith, having taught righteousness to the whole world, and come to the extreme limit of the west, and suffered martyrdom under the prefects.
entries.modernizedText: After preaching both in the east and west, he gained the illustrious reputation due to his faith, having taught righteousness to the whole world, and come to the farthest limit of the west, and suffered martyrdom under the prefects.

entries.originalText: Thus was he removed from the world, and went into the holy place, having proved himself a striking example of patience.
entries.modernizedText: Thus was he removed from the world, and went into the holy place, having proved himself a striking example of patience.

entries.originalText: To these men who spent their lives in the practice of holiness, there is to be added a great multitude of the elect, who, having through envy endured many indignities and tortures, furnished us with a most excellent example.
entries.modernizedText: To these men who spent their lives in the practice of holiness, there is to be added a great multitude of the elect, who, having through envy endured many indignities and tortures, furnished us with a most excellent example.

entries.originalText: Through envy, those women, the Danaids and Dircæ, being persecuted, after they had suffered terrible and unspeakable torments, finished the course of their faith with stedfastness, and though weak in body, received a noble reward.
entries.modernizedText: Through envy, those women, the Danaids and Dircae, being persecuted, after they had suffered terrible and unspeakable torments, completed the course of their faith with steadfastness, and although weak in body, received a noble reward.

entries.originalText: Envy has alienated wives from their husbands, and changed that saying of our father Adam, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh.”
entries.modernizedText: Envy has alienated wives from their husbands, and changed that saying of our father Adam, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh.”

entries.originalText: Envy and strife have overthrown great cities, and rooted up mighty nations.
entries.modernizedText: Envy and strife have overthrown great cities, and rooted up mighty nations.

entries.originalText: These things, beloved, we write unto you, not merely to admonish you of your duty, but also to remind ourselves.
entries.modernizedText: These things, beloved, we write to you, not merely to admonish you of your duty, but also to remind ourselves.

entries.originalText: For we are struggling on the same arena, and the same conflict is assigned to both of us.
entries.modernizedText: For we are struggling in the same arena, and the same conflict is assigned to both of us.

entries.originalText: Wherefore let us give up vain and fruitless cares, and approach to the glorious and venerable rule of our holy calling.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore let us give up vain and fruitless cares, and approach the glorious and venerable rule of our holy calling.

entries.originalText: Let us attend to what is good, pleasing, and acceptable in the sight of Him who formed us.
entries.modernizedText: Let us attend to what is good, pleasing, and acceptable in the sight of Him who formed us.

entries.originalText: Let us look stedfastly to the blood of Christ, and see how precious that blood is to God which, having been shed for our salvation, has set the grace of repentance before the whole world.
entries.modernizedText: Let us look steadfastly to the blood of Christ, and see how precious that blood is to God which, having been shed for our salvation, has set the grace of repentance before the whole world.

entries.originalText: Let us turn to every age that has passed, and learn that, from generation to generation, the Lord has granted a place of repentance to all such as would be converted unto Him.
entries.modernizedText: Let us turn to every age that has passed, and learn that, from generation to generation, the Lord has granted a place of repentance to all who would be converted to Him.

entries.originalText: Noah preached repentance, and as many as listened to him were saved.
entries.modernizedText: Noah preached repentance, and as many as listened to him were saved.

entries.originalText: Jonah proclaimed destruction to the Ninevites; but they, repenting of their sins, propitiated God by prayer, and obtained salvation, although they were aliens [to the covenant] of God.
entries.modernizedText: Jonah proclaimed destruction to the Ninevites; but they, repenting of their sins, propitiated God by prayer, and obtained salvation, although they were aliens [to the covenant] of God.

entries.originalText: The ministers of the grace of God have, by the Holy Spirit, spoken of repentance; and the Lord of all things has himself declared with an oath regarding it, “As I live, saith the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner, but rather his repentance;” adding, moreover, this gracious declaration, “Repent, O house of Israel, of your iniquity.”
entries.modernizedText: The ministers of the grace of God have, by the Holy Spirit, spoken of repentance; and the Lord of all things has himself declared with an oath regarding it, “As I live, says the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner, but rather his repentance;” adding, moreover, this gracious declaration, “Repent, O house of Israel, of your iniquity.”

entries.originalText: Say to the children of my people, Though your sins reach from earth to heaven, and though they be redder than scarlet, and blacker than sack-cloth, yet if ye turn to me with your whole heart, and say, Father!
entries.modernizedText: Say to my people, Though your sins reach from earth to heaven, and though they are redder than scarlet, and blacker than sackcloth, yet if you turn to me with your whole heart, and say, Father!

entries.originalText: I will listen to you, as to a holy people.
entries.modernizedText: I will listen to you, as to a holy people.

entries.originalText: And in another place He speaks thus: “Wash you and become clean; put away the wickedness of your souls from before mine eyes; cease from your evil ways, and learn to do well; seek out judgment, deliver the oppressed, judge the fatherless, and see that justice is done to the widow; and come, and let us reason together.
entries.modernizedText: And in another place He speaks thus: “Wash yourselves and become clean; put away the wickedness of your souls from before my eyes; cease from your evil ways, and learn to do well; seek out judgment, deliver the oppressed, judge the fatherless, and see that justice is done to the widow; and come, and let us reason together.

entries.originalText: He declares, Though your sins be like crimson, I will make them white as snow; though they be like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool.
entries.modernizedText: He declares, Though your sins are like crimson, I will make them white as snow; though they are like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool.

entries.originalText: And if ye be willing and obey me, ye shall eat the good of the land; but if ye refuse, and will not hearken unto me, the sword shall devour you, for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken these things.”
entries.modernizedText: And if you are willing and obey me, you shall eat the good of the land; but if you refuse, and will not listen to me, the sword shall devour you, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.”

entries.originalText: Desiring, therefore, that all His beloved should be partakers of repentance, He has, by His almighty will, established [these declarations].
entries.modernizedText: Desiring, therefore, that all His beloved should be partakers of repentance, He has, by His almighty will, established [these declarations].

entries.originalText: Wherefore, let us yield obedience to His excellent and glorious will; and imploring His mercy and loving-kindness, while we forsake all fruitless labours and strife, and envy, which leads to death, let us turn and have recourse to His compassions.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, let us yield obedience to His excellent and glorious will; and imploring His mercy and loving-kindness, while we forsake all fruitless labors and strife, and envy, which leads to death, let us turn and have recourse to His compassions.

entries.originalText: Let us stedfastly contemplate those who have perfectly ministered to his excellent glory.
entries.modernizedText: Let us steadfastly contemplate those who have perfectly ministered to his excellent glory.

entries.originalText: Let us take (for instance) Enoch, who, being found righteous in obedience, was translated, and death was never known to happen to him.
entries.modernizedText: Let us take (for instance) Enoch, who, being found righteous in obedience, was translated, and he was never known to die.

entries.originalText: Noah, being found faithful, preached regeneration to the world through his ministry; and the Lord saved by him the animals which, with one accord, entered into the ark.
entries.modernizedText: Noah, being found faithful, preached regeneration to the world through his ministry; and the Lord saved the animals through him which, with one accord, entered into the ark.

entries.originalText: Abraham, styled “the friend,” was found faithful, inasmuch as he rendered obedience to the words of God.
entries.modernizedText: Abraham, styled “the friend,” was found faithful, inasmuch as he rendered obedience to the words of God.

entries.originalText: He, in the exercise of obedience, went out from his own country, and from his kindred, and from his father’s house, in order that, by forsaking a small territory, and a weak family, and an insignificant house, he might inherit the promises of God.
entries.modernizedText: He, in the exercise of obedience, went out from his own country, and from his kindred, and from his father’s house, in order that, by forsaking a small territory, and a weak family, and an insignificant house, he might inherit the promises of God.

entries.originalText: For God said to him, “Get thee out from thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, into the land which I shall show thee.
entries.modernizedText: For God said to him, “Get you out from your country, and from your kindred, and from your father’s house, into the land which I shall show you.

entries.originalText: And I will make thee a great nation, and will bless thee, and make thy name great, and thou shalt be blessed.
entries.modernizedText: And I will make you a great nation, and will bless you, and make your name great, and you shall be blessed.

entries.originalText: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee; and in thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed.”
entries.modernizedText: And I will bless them that bless you, and curse them that curse you; and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed.”

entries.originalText: And again, on his departing from Lot, God said to him, “Lift up thine eyes, and look from the place where thou now art, northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward; for all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.
entries.modernizedText: And again, upon his departure from Lot, God said to him, “Lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you now are, northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward; for all the land which you see, to you will I give it, and to your seed forever.

entries.originalText: And I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth, [so that] if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed also be numbered.”
entries.modernizedText: And I will make your seed as the dust of the earth, [so that] if a man can number the dust of the earth, then your seed shall also be numbered.”

entries.originalText: And again [the Scripture] saith, “God brought forth Abram, and spake unto him, Look up now to heaven, and count the stars if thou be able to number them; so shall thy seed be.
entries.modernizedText: And again [the Scripture] says, “God brought forth Abram, and spoke to him, Look up now to heaven, and count the stars if you are able to number them; so shall your seed be.

entries.originalText: And Abram believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.”
entries.modernizedText: And Abram believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.”

entries.originalText: On account of his faith and hospitality, a son was given him in his old age; and in the exercise of obedience, he offered him as a sacrifice to God on one of the mountains which He showed him.
entries.modernizedText: On account of his faith and hospitality, a son was given to him in his old age; and in the exercise of obedience, he offered him as a sacrifice to God on one of the mountains which He showed him.

entries.originalText: On account of his hospitality and godliness, Lot was saved out of Sodom when all the country round was punished by means of fire and brimstone, the Lord thus making it manifest that He does not forsake those that hope in Him, but gives up such as depart from Him to punishment and torture.
entries.modernizedText: On account of his hospitality and godliness, Lot was saved out of Sodom when the surrounding country was punished by fire and brimstone, the Lord thus making it clear that He does not forsake those who hope in Him, but gives over those who depart from Him to punishment and torture.

entries.originalText: For Lot’s wife, who went forth with him, being of a different mind from himself, and not continuing in agreement with him [as to the command which had been given them], was made an example of, so as to be a pillar of salt unto this day.
entries.modernizedText: For Lot’s wife, who went forth with him, being of a different mind from himself, and not continuing in agreement with him [as to the command which had been given them], was made an example, becoming a pillar of salt to this day.

entries.originalText: This was done that all might know that those who are of a double mind, and who distrust the power of God, bring down judgment on themselves and become a sign to all succeeding generations.
entries.modernizedText: This was done that all might know that those who are of a double mind, and who distrust the power of God, bring down judgment on themselves and become a sign to all succeeding generations.

entries.originalText: On account of her faith and hospitality, Rahab the harlot was saved.
entries.modernizedText: On account of her faith and hospitality, Rahab the harlot was saved.

entries.originalText: For when spies were sent by Joshua, the son of Nun, to Jericho, the king of the country ascertained that they were come to spy out their land, and sent men to seize them, in order that, when taken, they might be put to death.
entries.modernizedText: For when spies were sent by Joshua, the son of Nun, to Jericho, the king of the country learned that they had come to spy out their land, and sent men to seize them, so that, when captured, they might be put to death.

entries.originalText: But the hospitable Rahab receiving them, concealed them on the roof of her house under some stalks of flax.
entries.modernizedText: But the hospitable Rahab received them and concealed them on the roof of her house under some stalks of flax.

entries.originalText: And when the men sent by the king arrived and said, “There came men unto thee who are to spy out our land; bring them forth, for so the king commands,” she answered them, “The two men whom ye seek came unto me, but quickly departed again and are gone,” thus not discovering the spies to them.
entries.modernizedText: And when the men sent by the king arrived and said, “There came men to you who are to spy out our land; bring them forth, for so the king commands,” she answered them, “The two men whom you seek came to me, but quickly departed again and are gone,” thus not discovering the spies to them.

entries.originalText: Then she said to the men, “I know assuredly that the Lord your God hath given you this city, for the fear and dread of you have fallen on its inhabitants.
entries.modernizedText: Then she said to the men, “I know for certain that the Lord your God has given you this city, for the fear and dread of you have fallen on its inhabitants.

entries.originalText: When therefore ye shall have taken it, keep ye me and the house of my father in safety.”
entries.modernizedText: When, therefore, you have taken it, keep me and the house of my father in safety.”

entries.originalText: And they said to her, “It shall be as thou hast spoken to us.
entries.modernizedText: And they said to her, “It shall be as you have spoken to us.

entries.originalText: As soon, therefore, as thou knowest that we are at hand, thou shalt gather all thy family under thy roof, and they shall be preserved, but all that are found outside of thy dwelling shall perish.”
entries.modernizedText: As soon, therefore, as you know that we are nearby, you shall gather all your family under your roof, and they shall be preserved, but all that are found outside of your dwelling shall perish.”

entries.originalText: Moreover, they gave her a sign to this effect, that she should hang forth from her house a scarlet thread.
entries.modernizedText: Moreover, they gave her a sign to this effect, that she should hang from her house a scarlet thread.

entries.originalText: And thus they made it manifest that redemption should flow through the blood of the Lord to all them that believe and hope in God.
entries.modernizedText: And thus they made it manifest that redemption should flow through the blood of the Lord to all who believe and hope in God.

entries.originalText: Ye see, beloved, that there was not only faith, but prophecy, in this woman.
entries.modernizedText: You see, beloved, that there was not only faith, but prophecy, in this woman.

entries.originalText: Let us therefore, brethren, be of humble mind, laying aside all haughtiness, and pride, and foolishness, and angry feelings; and let us act according to that which is written (for the Holy Spirit saith, “Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, neither let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him that glorieth glory in the Lord, in diligently seeking Him, and doing judgment and righteousness”), being especially mindful of the words of the Lord Jesus which He spake teaching us meekness and long-suffering.
entries.modernizedText: Let us therefore, brethren, be of humble mind, laying aside all haughtiness, and pride, and foolishness, and angry feelings; and let us act according to that which is written (for the Holy Spirit says, “Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, neither let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in the Lord, in diligently seeking Him, and doing judgment and righteousness”), being especially mindful of the words of the Lord Jesus which He spoke to teach us meekness and long-suffering.

entries.originalText: For thus He spoke: “Be ye merciful, that ye may obtain mercy; forgive, that it may be forgiven to you; as ye do, so shall it be done unto you; as ye judge, so shall ye be judged; as ye are kind, so shall kindness be shown to you; with what measure ye mete, with the same it shall be measured to you.”
entries.modernizedText: For thus He spoke: “Be merciful, that you may obtain mercy; forgive, that it may be forgiven to you; as you do, so shall it be done to you; as you judge, so shall you be judged; as you are kind, so shall kindness be shown to you; with what measure you use, with the same it shall be measured to you.”

entries.originalText: By this precept and by these rules let us stablish ourselves, that we walk with all humility in obedience to His holy words.
entries.modernizedText: By this precept and by these rules let us establish ourselves, so that we walk with all humility in obedience to His holy words.

entries.originalText: For the holy word saith, “On whom shall I look, but on him that is meek and peaceable, and that trembleth at my words?”
entries.modernizedText: For the holy word says, “On whom shall I look, but on him that is meek and peaceable, and that trembles at my words?”

entries.originalText: It is right and holy therefore, men and brethren, rather to obey God than to follow those who, through pride and sedition, have become the leaders of a detestable emulation.
entries.modernizedText: It is right and holy therefore, men and brethren, rather to obey God than to follow those who, through pride and sedition, have become the leaders of detestable rivalry.

entries.originalText: For we shall incur no slight injury, but rather great danger, if we rashly yield ourselves to the inclinations of men who aim at exciting strife and tumults, so as to draw us away from what is good.
entries.modernizedText: For we shall incur no slight injury, but rather great danger, if we rashly yield ourselves to the inclinations of men who aim at exciting strife and tumults, so as to draw us away from what is good.

entries.originalText: Let us be kind one to another after the pattern of the tender mercy and benignity of our Creator.
entries.modernizedText: Let us be kind one to another after the pattern of the tender mercy and benignity of our Creator.

entries.originalText: For it is written, “The kind-hearted shall inhabit the land, and the guiltless shall be left upon it, but transgressors shall be destroyed from off the face of it.”
entries.modernizedText: For it is written, “The kind-hearted shall inhabit the land, and the guiltless shall be left upon it, but transgressors shall be destroyed from the face of it.”

entries.originalText: And again [the Scripture] saith, “I saw the ungodly highly exalted, and lifted up like the cedars of Lebanon: I passed by, and, behold, he was not; and I diligently sought his place, and could not find it.
entries.modernizedText: And again [the Scripture] says, “I saw the ungodly highly exalted, and lifted up like the cedars of Lebanon: I passed by, and, behold, he was not; and I diligently sought his place, and could not find it.

entries.originalText: Preserve innocence, and look on equity: for there shall be a remnant to the peaceable man.”
entries.modernizedText: Preserve innocence, and look on equity: for there shall be a remnant to the peaceable man.”

entries.originalText: Let us cleave, therefore, to those who cultivate peace with godliness, and not to those who hypocritically profess to desire it.
entries.modernizedText: Let us cleave, therefore, to those who cultivate peace with godliness, and not to those who hypocritically profess to desire it.

entries.originalText: For [the Scripture] saith in a certain place, “This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.”
entries.modernizedText: For [the Scripture] says in a certain place, “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.”

entries.originalText: And again: “They bless with their mouth, but curse with their heart.”
entries.modernizedText: And again: “They bless with their mouth, but curse with their heart.”

entries.originalText: And again it saith, “They loved Him with their month, and lied to Him with their tongue; but their heart was not right with Him, neither were they faithful in His covenant.”
entries.modernizedText: And again it says, “They loved Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue; but their heart was not right with Him, neither were they faithful in His covenant.”

entries.originalText: “Let the deceitful lips become silent, [and “let the Lord destroy all the lying lips,] and the boastful tongue of those who have said, Let us magnify our tongue: our lips are our own; who is lord over us?
entries.modernizedText: “Let the deceitful lips become silent, [and “let the Lord destroy all the lying lips,] and the boastful tongue of those who have said, Let us magnify our tongue: our lips are our own; who is lord over us?

entries.originalText: For the oppression of the poor, and for the sighing of the needy, will I now arise, saith the Lord: I will place him in safety; I will deal confidently with him.”
entries.modernizedText: For the oppression of the poor, and for the sighing of the needy, will I now arise, says the Lord: I will place him in safety; I will deal confidently with him.”

entries.originalText: For Christ is of those who are humble-minded, and not of those who exalt themselves over His flock.
entries.modernizedText: For Christ is of those who are humble-minded, and not of those who exalt themselves over His flock.

entries.originalText: Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Sceptre of the majesty of God, did not come in the pomp of pride or arrogance, although He might have done so, but in a lowly condition, as the Holy Spirit had declared regarding Him.
entries.modernizedText: Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Scepter of the majesty of God, did not come in the pomp of pride or arrogance, although He might have done so, but in a lowly condition, as the Holy Spirit had declared regarding Him.

entries.originalText: For He says, “Lord, who hath believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?
entries.modernizedText: For He says, “Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?

entries.originalText: We have declared [our message] in His presence: He is, as it were, a child, and like a root in thirsty ground; He has no form nor glory, yea, we saw Him, and He had no form nor comeliness; but His form was without eminence, yea, deficient in comparison with the [ordinary] form of men.
entries.modernizedText: We have declared [our message] in His presence: He is, as it were, a child, and like a root in thirsty ground; He has no form nor glory, indeed, we saw Him, and He had no form nor comeliness; but His form was without eminence, indeed, deficient in comparison with the [ordinary] form of men.

entries.originalText: He is a man exposed to stripes and suffering, and acquainted with the endurance of grief: for His countenance was turned away; He was despised, and not esteemed.
entries.modernizedText: He is a man exposed to stripes and suffering, and acquainted with the endurance of grief: for His countenance was turned away; He was despised, and not esteemed.

entries.originalText: He bears our iniquities, and is in sorrow for our sakes; yet we supposed that [on His own account] He was exposed to labour, and stripes, and affliction.
entries.modernizedText: He bears our iniquities, and is in sorrow for our sakes; yet we supposed that [on His own account] He was exposed to labor, and stripes, and affliction.

entries.originalText: But He was wounded for our transgressions, and bruised for our iniquities.
entries.modernizedText: But He was wounded for our transgressions, and bruised for our iniquities.

entries.originalText: The chastisement of our peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we were healed.
entries.modernizedText: The chastisement of our peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we were healed.

entries.originalText: All we, like sheep, have gone astray; [every] man has wandered in his own way; and the Lord has delivered Him up for our sins, while He in the midst of His sufferings openeth not His mouth.
entries.modernizedText: All we, like sheep, have gone astray; [every] man has wandered in his own way; and the Lord has delivered Him up for our sins, while, in the midst of His sufferings, He does not open His mouth.

entries.originalText: He was brought as a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before her shearer is dumb, so He openeth not His mouth.
entries.modernizedText: He was brought as a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before her shearer is silent, so He does not open His mouth.

entries.originalText: In His humiliation His judgment was taken away; who shall declare His generation? for His life is taken from the earth.
entries.modernizedText: In His humiliation His judgment was taken away; who shall declare His generation? for His life is taken from the earth.

entries.originalText: For the transgressions of my people was He brought down to death.
entries.modernizedText: For the transgressions of my people was He brought down to death.

entries.originalText: And I will give the wicked for His sepulchre, and the rich for His death, because He did no iniquity, neither was guile found in His mouth.
entries.modernizedText: And I will give the wicked for His sepulchre, and the rich for His death, because He did no iniquity, neither was guile found in His mouth.

entries.originalText: And the Lord is pleased to purify him by stripes.
entries.modernizedText: And the Lord is pleased to purify him by stripes.

entries.originalText: If ye make an offering for sin, your soul shall see a long-lived seed.
entries.modernizedText: If you make an offering for sin, your soul shall see a long-lived seed.

entries.originalText: And the Lord is pleased to relieve Him of the affliction of His soul, to show Him light, and to form Him with understanding, to justify the Just One who ministereth well to many; and He Himself shall carry their sins.
entries.modernizedText: And the Lord is pleased to relieve Him of the affliction of His soul, to show Him light, and to give Him understanding, to justify the Just One who ministers well to many; and He Himself shall carry their sins.

entries.originalText: On this account He shall inherit many, and shall divide the spoil of the strong; because His soul was delivered to death, and He was reckoned among the transgressors, and He bare the sins of many, and for their sins was He delivered.”
entries.modernizedText: On this account He shall inherit many, and shall divide the spoil of the strong; because His soul was delivered to death, and He was reckoned among the transgressors, and He bore the sins of many, and for their sins was He delivered.”

entries.originalText: And again He saith, “I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people.
entries.modernizedText: And again He says, “I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people.

entries.originalText: All that see me have derided me; they have spoken with their lips; they have wagged their head, [saying] He hoped in God, let Him deliver Him, let Him save Him, since He delighteth in Him.”
entries.modernizedText: All that see me have derided me; they have spoken with their lips; they have wagged their head, [saying] He hoped in God, let Him deliver Him, let Him save Him, since He delights in Him.”

entries.originalText: Ye see, beloved, what is the example which has been given us; for if the Lord thus humbled Himself, what shall we do who have through Him come under the yoke of His grace?
entries.modernizedText: You see, beloved, what example has been given to us; for if the Lord thus humbled Himself, what shall we do who have through Him come under the yoke of His grace?

entries.originalText: Let us be imitators also of those who in goat-skins and sheep-skins went about proclaiming the coming of Christ; I mean Elijah, Elisha, and Ezekiel among the prophets, with those others to whom a like testimony is borne [in Scripture].
entries.modernizedText: Let us be imitators also of those who in goatskins and sheepskins went about proclaiming the coming of Christ; I mean Elijah, Elisha, and Ezekiel among the prophets, with those others to whom a like testimony is borne [in Scripture].

entries.originalText: Abraham was specially honoured, and was called the friend of God; yet he, earnestly regarding the glory of God, humbly declared, “I am but dust and ashes.”
entries.modernizedText: Abraham was specially honored, and was called the friend of God; yet he, earnestly regarding the glory of God, humbly declared, “I am but dust and ashes.”

entries.originalText: Moreover, it is thus written of Job, “Job was a righteous man, and blameless, truthful, God-fearing, and one that kept himself from all evil.”
entries.modernizedText: Moreover, it is thus written of Job, “Job was a righteous man, and blameless, truthful, God-fearing, and one who kept himself from all evil.”

entries.originalText: But bringing an accusation against himself, he said, “No man is free from defilement, even if his life be but of one day.”
entries.modernizedText: But bringing an accusation against himself, he said, “No man is free from defilement, even if his life is only one day old.”

entries.originalText: Moses was called faithful in all God’s house; and through his instrumentality, God punished Egypt with plagues and tortures.
entries.modernizedText: Moses was called faithful in all God’s house; and through him, God punished Egypt with plagues and tortures.

entries.originalText: Yet he, though thus greatly honoured, did not adopt lofty language, but said, when the divine oracle came to him out of the bush, “Who am I, that Thou sendest me?
entries.modernizedText: Yet he, though thus greatly honored, did not adopt lofty language, but said, when the divine oracle came to him out of the bush, “Who am I, that You send me?

entries.originalText: I am a man of a feeble voice and a slow tongue.”
entries.modernizedText: I am a man of a feeble voice and a slow tongue.”

entries.originalText: And again he said, “I am but as the smoke of a pot.”
entries.modernizedText: And again he said, “I am but as the smoke of a pot.”

entries.originalText: But what shall we say concerning David, to whom such testimony was borne, and of whom God said, “I have found a man after mine own heart, David the son of Jesse; and in everlasting mercy have I anointed him?”
entries.modernizedText: But what shall we say concerning David, to whom such testimony was borne, and of whom God said, “I have found a man after my own heart, David the son of Jesse; and in everlasting mercy have I anointed him?”

entries.originalText: Yet this very man saith to God, “Have mercy on me, O Lord, according to Thy great mercy; and according to the multitude of Thy compassions, blot out my transgression.
entries.modernizedText: Yet this very man says to God, “Have mercy on me, O Lord, according to Your great mercy; and according to the multitude of Your compassions, blot out my transgression.

entries.originalText: Wash me still more from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
entries.modernizedText: Wash me still more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.

entries.originalText: For I acknowledge mine iniquity, and my sin is ever before me.
entries.modernizedText: For I acknowledge my iniquity, and my sin is ever before me.

entries.originalText: Against Thee only have I sinned, and done that which is evil in Thy sight; that Thou mayest be justified in Thy sayings, and mayest overcome when Thou art judged.
entries.modernizedText: Against You only have I sinned, and done that which is evil in Your sight; that You may be justified in Your sayings, and may overcome when You are judged.

entries.originalText: For, behold, I was conceived in transgressions, and in sins did my mother conceive me.
entries.modernizedText: For, behold, I was conceived in transgressions, and in sins did my mother conceive me.

entries.originalText: For, behold, Thou hast loved truth; the secret and hidden things of wisdom hast Thou shown me.
entries.modernizedText: For, behold, You have loved truth; the secret and hidden things of wisdom have You shown me.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
entries.modernizedText: You shall sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; You shall wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt make me to hear joy and gladness; my bones, which have been humbled, shall exult.
entries.modernizedText: You shall make me to hear joy and gladness; my bones, which have been humbled, shall exult.

entries.originalText: Turn away Thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.
entries.modernizedText: Turn away Your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.

entries.originalText: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
entries.modernizedText: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

entries.originalText: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.
entries.modernizedText: Cast me not away from Your presence, and take not Your Holy Spirit from me.

entries.originalText: Restore to me the joy of Thy salvation, and establish me by Thy governing Spirit.
entries.modernizedText: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and establish me by Your governing Spirit.

entries.originalText: I will teach transgressors Thy ways, and the ungodly shall be converted unto Thee.
entries.modernizedText: I will teach transgressors Your ways, and the ungodly shall be converted to You.

entries.originalText: Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation: my tongue shall exult in Thy righteousness.
entries.modernizedText: Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation: my tongue shall exult in Your righteousness.

entries.originalText: O Lord, Thou shalt open my mouth, and my lips shall show forth Thy praise.
entries.modernizedText: O Lord, You shall open my mouth, and my lips shall show forth Your praise.

entries.originalText: For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would have given it; Thou wilt not delight in burnt-offerings.
entries.modernizedText: For if You had desired sacrifice, I would have given it; You will not delight in burnt-offerings.

entries.originalText: The sacrifice [acceptable] to God is a bruised spirit; a broken and a contrite heart God will not despise.”
entries.modernizedText: The sacrifice [acceptable] to God is a bruised spirit; a broken and a contrite heart God will not despise.”

entries.originalText: Thus the humility and godly submission of so great and illustrious men have rendered not only us, but also all the generations before us, better; even as many as have received His oracles in fear and truth.
entries.modernizedText: Thus the humility and godly submission of so great and illustrious men have made not only us but also all the generations before us better; even as many as have received His oracles in fear and truth.

entries.originalText: Wherefore, having so many great and glorious examples set before us, let us turn again to the practice of that peace which from the beginning was the mark set before us; and let us look stedfastly to the Father and Creator of the universe, and cleave to His mighty and surpassingly great gifts and benefactions of peace.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, having so many great and glorious examples set before us, let us turn again to the practice of that peace which from the beginning was the standard set before us; and let us look steadfastly to the Father and Creator of the universe, and cleave to His mighty and surpassingly great gifts and benefactions of peace.

entries.originalText: Let us contemplate Him with our understanding, and look with the eyes of our soul to His long-suffering will.
entries.modernizedText: Let us contemplate Him with our understanding, and look with the eyes of our soul to His long-suffering will.

entries.originalText: Let us reflect how free from the wrath He is towards all His creation.
entries.modernizedText: Let us reflect how free from wrath He is towards all His creation.

entries.originalText: The heavens, revolving under His government, are subject to Him in peace.
entries.modernizedText: The heavens, revolving under His government, are subject to Him in peace.

entries.originalText: Day and night run the course appointed by Him, in no wise hindering each other.
entries.modernizedText: Day and night run the course appointed by Him, in no way hindering each other.

entries.originalText: The sun and moon, with the companies of the stars, roll on in harmony according to His command, within their prescribed limits, and without any deviation.
entries.modernizedText: The sun and moon, with the constellations, roll on in harmony according to His command, within their prescribed limits, and without any deviation.

entries.originalText: The fruitful earth, according to His will, brings forth food in abundance, at the proper seasons, for man and beast and all the living beings upon it, never hesitating, nor changing any of the ordinances which He has fixed.
entries.modernizedText: The fruitful earth, according to His will, brings forth food in abundance, at the proper seasons, for man and beast and all the living beings upon it, never hesitating, nor changing any of the ordinances which He has fixed.

entries.originalText: The unsearchable places of abysses, and the indescribable arrangements of the lower world, are restrained by the same laws.
entries.modernizedText: The unsearchable depths of the abyss, and the indescribable workings of the lower world, are restrained by the same laws.

entries.originalText: The vast unmeasurable sea, gathered together by His working into various basins, never passes beyond the bounds placed around it, but does as He has commanded.
entries.modernizedText: The vast unmeasurable sea, gathered by His work into various basins, never passes beyond the bounds placed around it, but does as He has commanded.

entries.originalText: For He said, “Thus far shalt thou come, and thy waves shall be broken within thee.”
entries.modernizedText: For He said, “Thus far shall you come, and your waves shall be broken within you.”

entries.originalText: The ocean, impassable to man and the worlds beyond it, are regulated by the same enactments of the Lord.
entries.modernizedText: The ocean, impassable to man, and the lands beyond it, are regulated by the same enactments of the Lord.

entries.originalText: The seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, peacefully give place to one another.
entries.modernizedText: The seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, peacefully give way to one another.

entries.originalText: The winds in their several quarters fulfil, at the proper time, their service without hindrance.
entries.modernizedText: The winds in their several quarters fulfill, at the proper time, their service without hindrance.

entries.originalText: The ever-flowing fountains, formed both for enjoyment and health, furnish without fail their breasts for the life of men.
entries.modernizedText: The ever-flowing fountains, formed both for enjoyment and health, unfailingly provide their waters for human life.

entries.originalText: The very smallest of living beings meet together in peace and concord.
entries.modernizedText: The very smallest of living beings meet together in peace and concord.

entries.originalText: All these the great Creator and Lord of all has appointed to exist in peace and harmony; while He does good to all, but most abundantly to us who have fled for refuge to His compassions through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom be glory and majesty for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: All these the great Creator and Lord of all has appointed to exist in peace and harmony; while He does good to all, but most abundantly to us who have fled for refuge to His compassions through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom be glory and majesty forever and ever.

entries.originalText: Take heed, beloved, lest His many kindnesses lead to the condemnation of us all.
entries.modernizedText: Take heed, beloved, lest His many kindnesses lead to the condemnation of us all.

entries.originalText: [For thus it must be] unless we walk worthy of Him, and with one mind do those things which are good and well-pleasing in His sight.
entries.modernizedText: [For thus it must be] unless we walk worthy of Him, and with one mind do those things which are good and well-pleasing in His sight.

entries.originalText: For [the Scripture] saith in a certain place, “The Spirit of the Lord is a candle searching the secret parts of the belly.”
entries.modernizedText: For [the Scripture] says in a certain place, “The Spirit of the Lord is a candle searching the secret parts of the belly.”

entries.originalText: Let us reflect how near He is, and that none of the thoughts or reasonings in which we engage are hid from Him.
entries.modernizedText: Let us reflect how near He is, and that none of the thoughts or reasonings in which we engage are hidden from Him.

entries.originalText: It is right, therefore, that we should not leave the post which His will has assigned us.
entries.modernizedText: It is right, therefore, that we should not leave the position which His will has assigned us.

entries.originalText: Let us rather offend those men who are foolish, and inconsiderate, and lifted up, and who glory in the pride of their speech, than [offend] God.
entries.modernizedText: Let us rather offend those men who are foolish, and inconsiderate, and lifted up, and who glory in the pride of their speech, than [offend] God.

entries.originalText: Let us reverence the Lord Jesus Christ, whose blood was given for us; let us esteem those who have the rule over us; let us honour the aged among us; let us train up the young men in the fear of God; let us direct our wives to that which is good.
entries.modernizedText: Let us reverence the Lord Jesus Christ, whose blood was given for us; let us esteem those who have the rule over us; let us honor the aged among us; let us train up the young men in the fear of God; let us direct our wives to that which is good.

entries.originalText: Let them exhibit the lovely habit of purity [in all their conduct]; let them show forth the sincere disposition of meekness; let them make manifest the command which they have of their tongue, by their manner of speaking; let them display their love, not by preferring one to another, but by showing equal affection to all that piously fear God.
entries.modernizedText: Let them exhibit the lovely habit of purity [in all their conduct]; let them show forth the sincere disposition of meekness; let them make manifest the control they have over their tongue, by their manner of speaking; let them display their love, not by preferring one to another, but by showing equal affection to all that piously fear God.

entries.originalText: Let your children be partakers of true Christian training; let them learn of how great avail humility is with God—how much the spirit of pure affection can prevail with Him—how excellent and great His fear is, and how it saves all those who walk in it with a pure mind.
entries.modernizedText: Let your children be partakers of true Christian training; let them learn of how greatly humility avails with God—how much a spirit of pure affection can prevail with Him—how excellent and great His fear is, and how it saves all those who walk in it with a pure mind.

entries.originalText: For He is a Searcher of the thoughts and desires [of the heart]: His breath is in us; and when He pleases, He will take it away.
entries.modernizedText: For He is a Searcher of the thoughts and desires [of the heart]: His breath is in us; and when He pleases, He will take it away.
